fullPassage:
Sweet Success: Lemonade Stand Economics

Author: Luke Peres
President of The Helpers, the school's biggest volunteer club

High school is not only where we study different subjects but also where we learn about life. We are a group of students that get together every week to discuss ways to make a difference in our society. In this newsletter, I would like to share the story of how we participated in our community's international food festival. On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan. Here is our story.

Setting Up Our Plans
Choosing What to Sell:
The first step we took was to decide what to sell. Some of the ideas that we discussed included cotton candy, corn dogs, and lemonade. Out of these options, we agreed that a lemonade stand would be the easiest for us, as we would need only a good recipe and a few ingredients. We also found out that no other stand had signed up to sell drinks, so lemonade seemed to be the natural choice.

Finding the Perfect Recipe:
Once we decided on lemonade, we needed the perfect recipe. Fortunately, we were able to find a simple one online. We just needed freshly squeezed lemons, sugar, water, and ice. After trying out different variations of the recipe on friends and family, we decided on the final recipe. It would make about 1.5 liters of lemonade, which could be sold as five cups.

Pricing
The main goal of setting up the lemonade stand was to make enough profit for a donation to the local children's home. To maximize our profit, we needed to decrease our costs and increase our revenue.

Profit Formula
PROFIT = REVENUE - COSTS

Costs:
Since we wanted to minimize costs, our first step was to find the most affordable ingredients and cups available. As we were researching prices, we found that buying ingredients and cups in bulk would be the smartest way to go. The chart below shows how much we could save by buying in bulk.

Revenue and Profit:
Now that we had found out how to minimize costs, we needed to decide on a reasonable price for a cup of lemonade. We contacted a festival organizer to gather information. First, we inquired about the previous year's drink prices, and she told us that soft drinks had been sold for $1.50 per cup. Considering that freshly squeezed lemonade usually costs more, we decided to sell each cup for $2. Based on our recipe and the costs of the ingredients and cups, each cup of lemonade would cost us about $0.70 to make. With a selling price of $2, we expected a profit of $1.30 per cup.

Regarding attendance, we learned that the festival organizers were expecting around 400 people for each of the two days of the festival. We thought we could reasonably sell lemonade to half of the people attending, so we aimed to sell 400 cups over the two days. If we could do that, our revenue would amount to $800!

However, this revenue wouldn't be pure profit. We needed to subtract our costs from it. In addition to the cost of $280 required to make 400 cups, we also had to factor in the $6 we needed for posters and fliers. If we reached our goal, we would be able to make $514 in profit. That would be a big donation!

Marketing
Location-Based Marketing:
When the organizer asked us where we wanted our stand, we knew that location was going to be important. She sent us a map showing which foods were going to be sold at which stands, and we chose an opening between the tteokbokki and spicy kebab stands. Who could resist a cool, sweet lemonade after some spicy and salty food?

Our Marketing Strategies:
Developing marketing strategies to attract more customers was the most enjoyable part. In addition to designing posters and fliers, we also explored various online marketing techniques. One of our club members suggested we offer customers free refills for mentioning our stand on their social media accounts. We all agreed that was a great way to spread the word. We also planned to install a photo zone and give coupons for a 10% discount to customers who posted photos they took there with the tag "#sweetsuccess," the name of our stand.

The Results
Mission completed! Our lemonade stand was a huge success! Because of the hot weather, we ended up purchasing extra bags of ice. We also had to give free refills and discounts to some customers, which we did as part of our marketing strategy. Even with these extra costs, however, we were still able to make a profit of $479. Even though we couldn't reach our profit goal, we were happy that we were able to make a big donation to the children's home. We also learned a valuable lesson in economics, a lesson we never could have learned in the classroom!

questions.passage: High school is not only where we study different subjects but also where we learn about life. We are a group of students that get together every week to discuss ways to make a (A)[difference / similarity] in our society. In this newsletter, I would like to share the story of how we (B)[participated / withdrew] in our community's international food festival. On top of raising enough money to make a (C)[donation / profit], we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 사회에 변화를(difference) 가져오기 위해, 축제에 참여했고(participated), 기부(donation)를 위한 돈을 모았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① difference — participated — donation: 원문 일치
❌ ② similarity(유사성): make a difference(변화를 만들다)가 원문
❌ ③ withdrew(철수했다): participated의 반의어
❌ ④ profit(이익): donation(기부)이 원문. 마지막에 profit도 나오지만 여기서는 donation
det.tip: make a difference = 변화를 만들다, 차이를 가져오다. participate in = ~에 참여하다.

questions.passage: The main goal of setting up the lemonade stand was to make enough profit for a donation to the local children's home. To (A)[maximize / minimize] our profit, we needed to (B)[decrease / increase] our costs and increase our revenue. Since we wanted to minimize costs, our first step was to find the most (C)[affordable / expensive] ingredients and cups available.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이익을 극대화(maximize)하기 위해 비용을 줄이고(decrease), 가장 저렴한(affordable) 재료를 찾았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ maximize — decrease — affordable: 원문 일치
❌ ① increase costs: 비용을 늘리면 이익이 줄어듦
❌ ② minimize profit: 이익을 최소화는 목표에 반함
❌ ④ expensive: 저렴한 재료를 찾는 맥락에 반대
det.tip: maximize profit = 이익 극대화. decrease costs = 비용 절감. affordable = 가격이 적당한, 저렴한.

questions.passage: Developing marketing strategies to attract more customers was the most (A)[enjoyable / tedious] part. One of our club members suggested we offer customers free refills for mentioning our stand on their social media accounts. We all agreed that was a great way to (B)[spread / contain] the word. We also planned to install a photo zone and give coupons for a 10% discount to customers who posted photos. Even with these extra costs, however, we were still able to make a (C)[profit / loss] of $479.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 가장 즐거운(enjoyable) 부분이었고, 입소문을 퍼뜨리는(spread) 방법이었으며, $479의 이익(profit)을 냈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② enjoyable — spread — profit: 원문 일치
❌ ① contain(억제하다): spread의 반의어
❌ ③ tedious(지루한): enjoyable의 반의어
❌ ④ loss(손실): profit의 반의어
det.tip: spread the word = 입소문을 내다. enjoyable(즐거운) ↔ tedious(지루한). profit(이익) ↔ loss(손실).

questions.passage: The first step we took was to decide what to sell. Some of the ideas that we discussed included cotton candy, corn dogs, and lemonade. Out of these ①<u>options</u>, we agreed that a lemonade stand would be the ②<u>easiest</u> for us, as we would need only a good recipe and a few ③<u>ingredients</u>. We also found out that no other stand had signed up to sell drinks, so lemonade seemed to be the ④<u>artificial</u> choice.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '자연스러운(natural)'인데 '인위적인(artificial)'으로 바뀌었다. 다른 음료 가판대가 없어서 자연스러운 선택이었다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① options(선택지): 원문 일치
✅ ② easiest(가장 쉬운): 원문 일치
✅ ③ ingredients(재료): 원문 일치
❌ ④ artificial(인위적인) → natural(자연스러운): 반의어 교체
det.tip: natural choice = 자연스러운 선택 ↔ artificial choice = 인위적인 선택.

questions.passage: Now that we had found out how to minimize costs, we needed to decide on a ①<u>reasonable</u> price for a cup of lemonade. We contacted a festival organizer to ②<u>gather</u> information. Considering that freshly squeezed lemonade usually costs more, we decided to sell each cup for $2. However, this revenue wouldn't be ③<u>pure</u> profit. We needed to ④<u>add</u> our costs from it.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '빼다(subtract)'인데 '더하다(add)'로 바뀌었다. 수익에서 비용을 빼야 순이익이 된다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reasonable(합리적인): 원문 일치
✅ ② gather(수집하다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ pure(순수한): 원문 일치
❌ ④ add(더하다) → subtract(빼다): 반의어 교체. PROFIT = REVENUE - COSTS
det.tip: subtract(빼다) ↔ add(더하다). 이익 = 수익 - 비용이므로 subtract가 맞다.

questions.passage: When the organizer asked us where we wanted our stand, we knew that ①<u>location</u> was going to be important. She sent us a map showing which foods were going to be sold at which stands, and we chose an opening between the tteokbokki and spicy kebab stands. Who could ②<u>resist</u> a cool, sweet lemonade after some spicy and salty food? In addition to designing posters and fliers, we also ③<u>explored</u> various online marketing techniques. Even though we couldn't reach our profit goal, we were happy that we were able to make a big ④<u>withdrawal</u> to the children's home.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '기부(donation)'인데 '출금(withdrawal)'로 바뀌었다. 보육원에 기부했다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① location(위치): 원문 일치
✅ ② resist(참다, 저항하다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ explored(탐색했다): 원문 일치
❌ ④ withdrawal(출금, 철수) → donation(기부): 의미 반대
det.tip: donation(기부) ↔ withdrawal(출금, 인출). 보육원에 기부(donation)를 했다는 문맥.

questions.passage: High school is not only where we study different subjects but also where we learn about life. We are a group of students that get together every week to discuss ways to make a difference in our society. The first step we took was to decide what to sell. Some of the ideas that we discussed included cotton candy, corn dogs, and lemonade. Out of these options, we agreed that a lemonade stand would be the easiest for us, as we would need only a good __________ and a few ingredients.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 좋은 조리법(recipe)과 몇 가지 재료만 있으면 됐다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① recipe(조리법): 원문 일치. 레모네이드 만드는 방법
❌ ② budget(예산): 재료(ingredients)와 병렬인 것은 recipe
❌ ③ sponsor(후원자): 맥락 없음
❌ ④ permit(허가): 허가 이야기는 없음
det.tip: recipe(조리법, 레시피) + ingredients(재료) = 음식을 만들기 위한 기본 요소.

questions.passage: The main goal of setting up the lemonade stand was to make enough profit for a donation to the local children's home. To maximize our profit, we needed to decrease our costs and increase our revenue. Since we wanted to minimize costs, our first step was to find the most affordable ingredients and cups available. As we were researching prices, we found that buying ingredients and cups in __________ would be the smartest way to go. The chart below shows how much we could save by buying this way.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 재료와 컵을 대량으로(in bulk) 구매하는 것이 가장 현명한 방법이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ bulk(대량): 원문 일치. in bulk = 대량으로
❌ ① advance(미리): in advance = 사전에. 맥락과 맞지 않음
❌ ② secret(비밀): in secret = 비밀리에. 맥락 없음
❌ ④ person(직접): in person = 직접. 가격 절약 맥락에 안 맞음
det.tip: in bulk = 대량으로. buy in bulk = 대량 구매. 절약(save)과 연결되는 표현.

questions.passage: We contacted a festival organizer to gather information. First, we inquired about the previous year's drink prices, and she told us that soft drinks had been sold for $1.50 per cup. Considering that freshly squeezed lemonade usually costs more, we decided to sell each cup for $2. Based on our recipe and the costs of the ingredients and cups, each cup of lemonade would cost us about $0.70 to make. With a selling price of $2, we expected a __________ of $1.30 per cup.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 판매가 $2에서 원가 $0.70을 빼면 컵당 $1.30의 이익(profit)을 예상했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② profit(이익): $2 - $0.70 = $1.30 이익
❌ ① loss(손실): 판매가가 원가보다 높으므로 이익
❌ ③ refund(환불): 맥락 없음
❌ ④ debt(빚): 맥락 없음
det.tip: profit(이익) = revenue(수익) - costs(비용). $2.00 - $0.70 = $1.30.

questions.passage: We are a group of students that get together every week to discuss ways to make a difference in our society. In this newsletter, I would like to <u>share</u> the story of how we participated in our community's international food festival.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>share</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이야기를 나누다(share) = 이야기를 말하다(tell).
det.analysis:
✅ ② tell(말하다): share의 동의어. 이야기를 전달하다
❌ ① hide(숨기다): share의 반의어
❌ ③ keep(간직하다): 나누지 않고 갖고 있다
❌ ④ sell(팔다): 다른 의미
det.tip: share a story = tell a story = 이야기를 나누다/전하다.

questions.passage: Now that we had found out how to minimize costs, we needed to decide on a <u>reasonable</u> price for a cup of lemonade. We contacted a festival organizer to gather information.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>reasonable</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 레모네이드 한 컵의 합리적인(reasonable) 가격 = 공정한(fair) 가격.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ fair(공정한, 적정한): reasonable의 동의어
❌ ① excessive(과도한): 합리적의 반대
❌ ② random(무작위의): 맥락 무관
❌ ③ cheap(싼): 합리적은 싸다는 뜻이 아니라 적절하다는 뜻
det.tip: reasonable price = fair price = 적정 가격. reasonable ≠ cheap.

questions.passage: We also had to give free refills and discounts to some customers, which we did as part of our marketing strategy. Even with these extra costs, however, we were still able to make a profit of $479. We also learned a <u>valuable</u> lesson in economics.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>valuable</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 경제학에서의 귀중한(valuable) 교훈 = 소중한(precious) 교훈.
det.analysis:
✅ ① precious(소중한): valuable의 동의어
❌ ② worthless(가치 없는): valuable의 반의어
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): 귀중한과 다른 의미
❌ ④ temporary(일시적인): 다른 범주
det.tip: valuable = precious = priceless = 귀중한, 소중한.

questions.passage: Developing marketing strategies to <u>attract</u> more customers was the most enjoyable part. In addition to designing posters and fliers, we also explored various online marketing techniques.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>attract</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 더 많은 고객을 끌어들이기(attract) ↔ 쫓아내기(repel).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ repel(쫓아내다): attract의 반의어
❌ ① invite(초대하다): attract과 유사
❌ ② interest(흥미를 끌다): attract과 유사
❌ ④ impress(감동시키다): 긍정적 의미
det.tip: attract(끌다) ↔ repel(밀어내다). 자석의 N극과 S극처럼 반대.

questions.passage: Since we wanted to <u>minimize</u> costs, our first step was to find the most affordable ingredients and cups available.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>minimize</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 비용을 최소화(minimize) ↔ 극대화(maximize).
det.analysis:
✅ ① maximize(극대화하다): minimize의 정확한 반의어
❌ ② reduce(줄이다): minimize과 유사
❌ ③ limit(제한하다): minimize과 유사
❌ ④ control(통제하다): 다른 의미
det.tip: minimize(최소화) ↔ maximize(극대화). mini- ↔ maxi-.

questions.passage:
(A) On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business <u>plan</u>.
(B) We also <u>plan</u>ned to install a photo zone and give coupons for a 10% discount.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 plan이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) business plan = 사업 계획(명사). (B) planned to = 계획했다(동사).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 명사 — (B) 동사: (A)는 'a business plan'에서 명사, (B)는 'planned to install'에서 동사(과거형)
❌ ① (A)가 동사라면 'carry out a business plan'에서 plan이 목적어이므로 명사
❌ ② 설계도: 여기서는 사업 계획
❌ ④ 둘 다 동사: (A)는 명사
det.tip: plan: 명사(계획) / 동사(계획하다). 문맥에서 품사 구별.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"the money that you make in business when revenue exceeds costs"

det.korean: 수익이 비용을 초과할 때 사업으로 벌어들이는 돈 = 이익(profit).
det.analysis:
✅ ② profit(이익): 영영 풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ① revenue(수익): 전체 매출이지 이익이 아님
❌ ③ budget(예산): 계획된 지출이지 이익이 아님
❌ ④ expense(비용): 지출이지 이익이 아님
det.tip: profit = revenue - costs. revenue(수익) = 총 매출. profit(이익) = 순수익.

questions.passage: Developing marketing strategies to attract more customers was the most __________ (enjoy) part. In addition to designing posters and fliers, we also explored various online marketing techniques.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 가장 즐거운(enjoyable) 부분이었다.
det.analysis: enjoy(동사) → enjoyable(형용사): 'the most _____ part'에서 명사 수식 형용사 필요
det.tip: enjoy(동사) → enjoyable(형용사, 즐거운) → enjoyment(명사, 즐거움). -able = ~할 수 있는.

questions.passage: Once we decided on lemonade, we needed the perfect recipe. Fortunately, we were able to find a simple one online. We just needed __________ (fresh) squeezed lemons, sugar, water, and ice. After trying out different variations of the recipe on friends and family, we decided on the final recipe.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 갓(freshly) 짜낸 레몬이 필요했다.
det.analysis: fresh(형용사) → freshly(부사): squeezed(과거분사)를 수식하므로 부사 필요
det.tip: fresh(형용사, 신선한) → freshly(부사, 갓, 새로). freshly squeezed = 갓 짜낸.

questions.passage: When the organizer asked us where we wanted our stand, we knew that location was going to be important. She sent us a map showing which foods were going to be sold at which stands, and we chose an opening between the tteokbokki and spicy kebab stands. Developing marketing strategies to attract more customers was the most enjoyable part. In addition to designing posters and fliers, we also explored various online marketing techniques. Who could resist a cool, sweet lemonade __________?
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: after some spicy and salty food

det.korean: 맵고 짭짤한 음식을 먹고 난 후에(after some spicy and salty food) 시원한 레모네이드를 참을 수 있겠는가?
det.analysis:
✅ ④ after some spicy and salty food: 원문 일치. 떡볶이/케밥 사이에 위치한 이유
❌ ① 축제 시작 전: 시간 맥락 아님
